chunks: From him, from Ayyub, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the slave man who performs li'an with the free woman, he said: Yes, if his master had married her to him, he would perform li'an by the command of his master, and that would be the case. And he said: Between the free man and the slave woman, and between the Muslim man and the female dhimmi, there is li'an. And it is possible that this report came out as taqiyyah (prudent dissimulation), because among the opponents there are those who say there is no li'an between the free man and the slave woman.
ai.seo_question: Does li'an apply between a slave man and a free woman in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfabar establishes the validity of li'an between a free woman and her slave husband, provided the master consented to the marriage, while also noting the broader applicability to Muslim-dhimmi unions. The mention of taqiyyah reflects the historical juristic debate, particularly among those who restricted li'an to free-born pairings, highlighting the flexibility of Shia fiqh in accommodating varying social statuses within marital contracts.
